clue.text: To mend it later could be harmful

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of these words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone warns that putting off a repair could do damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MENDITLATER; 'To' is a link word, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detrimental causes damage, which is what harmful means.

clue.text: In a word, go by a swimmer

annotationWithheld.why: In a word, go by a swimmer (8): DRAG ON gives 'go by' (time drags on) but nothing in the clue as held supplies the closing ET; the clue looks garbled or cut short
annotationWithheld.clue: In a word, go by a swimmer

clue.text: Underwear in attempt to disguise

annotationWithheld.why: Underwear in attempt to disguise (8): VEST in TRY gives TRVESTY; the A of TRAVESTY has no clue word, so a word ('a') seems lost from the clue as held

clue.text: A preparer of hides doesn't enquire near bull!

indicators.note: doesn't says the following word's synonym is dropped from the phrase before it

parts.note: a skinner prepares animal hides, so with the article this is A SKINNER
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a leatherworker stays quiet when standing next to a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't' strips ASK from the front of A SKINNER. On a dartboard or archery target the inner is the ring next to the bull's-eye, so 'near bull' defines it; the bull is not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner ring lies directly around the bullseye of a target.

clue.text: One steeple oddly without point associated with St Paul

indicators.note: oddly says the letters are arranged in an odd, unexpected way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a point of the compass, here E for east

explanation.surface: A church steeple seen as strangely blunt, in a parish dedicated to St Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the E (a compass point) from I plus STEEPLE, and 'oddly' rearranges what is left. The New Testament letters of St Paul are his Epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul wrote many New Testament letters, so an epistle is a writing linked with him.

clue.text: The original motive for disloyalty

indicators.note: original points to the very beginning of the following word, its first letter

parts.note: a motive is a reason for acting

explanation.surface: Asking what first drove someone to betray their side.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: One may look through this at the 23

definitions.text: One may look through this at the 23

parts.words: One may look through this at the 23
parts.note: 23 is OPERA; the clue describes a small pair of glasses on a handle held up by a theatregoer

explanation.surface: A viewing aid used by someone in the audience at a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles on a handle, traditionally used at the theatre.

clue.text: Scottish couple. in West Wales

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A pair of Scots living in the west of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop in the clue as held is an OCR artefact. In Scots dialect twa means two.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word for two, so a pair.

clue.text: Skill returns to soldier about to be sad

indicators.note: returns says the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: skill is art
GI is an American soldier
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A talent coming back to a serviceman who is about to be miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something deeply unhappy, a stronger form of sad.

clue.text: Things to be done almost a danger?

annotationWithheld.why: Things to be done almost a danger? (6): A DANGE(R) rearranged gives the letters, but no clue word outside the definition signals the anagram; 'to be done' would have to be both definition and indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Things to be done almost a danger?

clue.text: On the other hand, a prophet say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be heard, so the sound of prophet stands for another word

parts.note: prophet sounds like profit, and profit is gain

explanation.surface: A seer offering a contrary view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes 'prophet' sound like 'profit', a synonym of GAIN. Again can mean 'besides' or 'on the other hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: Again can introduce a contrary point, as in 'then again', meaning however.

clue.text: He always has mine

parts.note: the drinker's order 'make mine a double': this man always says 'mine', ordering another

explanation.surface: Someone who always takes what is offered to him.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, always ready to order another drink.

clue.text: Paramour losing head values too much?

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter of the word for a paramour

parts.note: a paramour is a lover
to value is to rate, so values are rates

explanation.surface: A lover who has lost their head and prizes someone excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' turns LOVER into OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate is to think more highly of something than it deserves.

clue.text: Huntress transformed into a nymph

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the huntress's name change into a new form

parts.note: Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A myth in which a goddess of hunting is changed into a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges DIANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: President enters party to make 26

indicators.note: party to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A head of state joins talks to secure a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'make' as the definition; 'make' is a link word and the definition is '26', AGREEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an understanding between nations, a kind of accord.

clue.text: Modern oracle — not heartless shopkeeper

parts.note: modern means new
an oracle is a wise person, a sage

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word not

parts.note: taken as written before its centre goes

explanation.surface: A contemporary seer who turns out to be a cold-hearted trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the O out of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent keeps a shop selling papers and magazines.

clue.text: Fame for three out of four bridge players

definitions.text: three out of four bridge players

explanation.surface: Renown earned by most of a bridge four.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge players are North, East, South and West; three of them are 'not E(ast)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Note is distinction or renown; and reading 'not E' covers every player but East.

clue.text: An evil turn may be poisonous

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a wicked twist might prove toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges EVILTURN; 'An' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Virulent describes something highly toxic or infectious.

clue.text: Leading revolt on board to make headline

annotationWithheld.why: Leading revolt on board to make headline (8): no parse of the clue as held builds the letters from 'Leading revolt on board'
annotationWithheld.clue: Leading revolt on board to make headline

clue.text: Hands back in exchange

indicators.note: back says the word for hands is read in reverse

parts.note: paws are hands, informally

explanation.surface: Giving something back as part of a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PAWS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to give one thing in return for another.

clue.text: Return -of fishing gear in Newhaven is an omen

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Newhaven is a port on England's south coast

indicators.note: Return says the fishing gear is read backwards

parts.note: a net is fishing gear

explanation.surface: A trawler's nets coming back into a harbour town as a sign of things to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reads the net backwards before it goes into the port. Newhaven is a Sussex ferry port; the hyphen before 'of' is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign foretelling what is to come.

clue.text: Not quite the voice perhaps for the cloth

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the remaining letters could be ordered differently
not quite drops the final letter of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A clergyman's voice that is not quite right, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' removes the last E of THE VOICE and 'perhaps' rearranges THEVOIC. 'The cloth' usually means the clergy, but here 'cloth' is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheviot is a woollen fabric made from the wool of Cheviot sheep.

clue.text: Hop producer in state by the sea

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A hop farm in some state on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a kiln for drying hops, typical of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal describes land beside the shore.

clue.text: Discover look about goddess

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
C is short for circa, about
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Finding a deity by searching around.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find where it is.

clue.text: Typist's first mistake is a nuisance

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: a mistake is an error

explanation.surface: A typing slip that is a real bother.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'terror' is an annoying person, typically a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublesome child is called a little terror, a pest.

clue.text: Work time entertainment?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Asking whether working hours are for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical drama, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Spacious residence — not British to stay here

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation that follows is removed

parts.note: spacious means broad
a house is a residence

explanation.surface: A grand home that is not British, as a place to lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes the B off BROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn beside a main road, a place where travellers stay.

clue.text: Possessed by eastern sun — it leads to Abaddon

parts.note: possessed means had

explanation.surface: Someone possessed by an eastern sun god, on the road to destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Abaddon is a biblical name for the place of destruction in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the underworld, the realm leading to the abyss of the dead.

clue.text: May be reached after meeting

parts.note: talks or a meeting may end with both sides coming to terms

explanation.surface: Something that may come out of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides reach a settlement of terms after discussion.

clue.text: Made right form of fantasy

indicators.note: form of says the letters are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone shaping a daydream properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges MADE with R.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is an imagined scene, a fantasy.

clue.text: Plough handle

explanation.surface: A farming tool's grip.
explanation.definitionFit: To ear is an archaic verb meaning to till the soil; an ear is also a jug's lug or grip.

clue.text: Forecast here if on course

parts.note: a forecast is a type of racing bet; at the racecourse it is placed with the betting machine

explanation.surface: Where to make a prediction if you are on track.
explanation.walkthrough: A forecast is a bet naming the first two finishers; at the racecourse it is placed with the tote.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator is the pool-betting machine at a racecourse.
